title: I Let the Bar Tab Policy Hit the Regular Who Never Pays Until Close

parts.text: I picked up a Tuesday shift at 4:00. The regular, Cal, ran a tab with no card because "everyone knows me." The new policy in the binder said card at open of tab. I was twenty-four, bartender, holding a binder that still smelled like laminate. I asked Cal for a card. He said I was ruining the vibe. My manager, off tonight, texted: just let Cal ride. At 12:50 Cal ordered a round for strangers and walked toward the door. The POS blinked AUTHORIZE. There was nothing to authorize.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: He is walking out with a round for strangers and no card on a tab the binder forbade.

social.video_title: The regular ordered a walking round with no card — Part 1/2
social.description: Laminate binder, Tuesday shift, a vibe that does not swipe. Manager said let it ride. Would you have blocked the door?

parts.text: I did not block the door. I called out that house policy requires a card and the cameras face the rail. Cal came back, threw a card, signed like a martyr. The strangers still got their drinks. The tab closed. My manager later said I had been harsh. The binder was harsher. Cal now lays a card down at 4:05 like a person. The vibe survived. The register survived better. I keep the binder open to that page when he sits.

social.video_title: The rail camera convinced the martyr to swipe — Part 2/2
social.description: Tab closed, strangers served, card at 4:05. Was a vibe a credit line?
